board: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE (9-1) Islamic Studies (4IS1, paper 4IS1/01)
source: Gap-fill against Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Islamic Studies 4IS1 specification

lessons.unit: Unit 1.2: The Revelation of the Qur'an
lessons.title: Why the first revelation mattered in establishing Islam
lessons.bigQuestion: How did one night in a cave on Jabal al-Nur change the world?
objectives: Recall the events of the first revelation in Hira
Explain why this experience mattered for the Prophet and for the start of Islam
Link the first revelation to the beginning of the Prophet's mission
successCriteria: All: describe what happened at Hira
Most: give two reasons why it mattered
Some: evaluate its importance for the establishment of Islam
lessons.crossCurricular: History: the start of a movement and its first supporters
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: reflecting on the gift of guidance and the value of reading and learning

keywords.def: Allah's message communicated to a prophet
the angel who brought revelation to the prophets
the cave near Makkah where the Prophet used to reflect
the mission of delivering Allah's message
'read' or 'recite', the first command in the first revealed verses

starter: Bismillah. Who was the Prophet's first wife and what is she known for?
Name the month of the Night of Power.

teach.heading: What happened
bullets: The Prophet reflected in the cave of Hira in Ramadan.
Jibril came and commanded him to read.
The Prophet returned frightened and told Khadijah.
teach.note: Recap briefly; pupils studied the event in the lesson on the Night of Power. Keep to what is widely reported: Jibril appeared, the command was iqra, and the Prophet returned home trembling. Stress we narrate with respect and say 'peace be upon him' after his name. The date and details vary slightly in reports; say so where unsure. Teacher note: every Qur'an reference here is marked verify; check the surah and ayah numbers and the translation against a trusted mushaf and translation before the lesson.

quote.text: Read in the name of your Lord who created. (Qur'an 96:1, verify)

teach.heading: Reassurance and the first believers
teach.note: Khadijah reassured him by listing his good character (trustworthy, kind to kin, helped the needy). She took him to her cousin Waraqa ibn Nawfal who was familiar with earlier scriptures and said the angel was the same one who came to Musa. Ask: why was her support important? Avoid inventing wording; paraphrase only. Early believers included Khadijah, Ali, Zayd ibn Harithah and Abu Bakr (reports differ on order; say 'among the first').

teach.heading: Why it mattered: for the Prophet
bullets: It began his prophethood and his mission.
It gave him certainty that Allah had chosen him.
It started the Qur'an, a guide for all people.
teach.note: Emphasise that this experience started the revelation that continued for about 23 years. The Prophet moved from reflection to responsibility. The first word, iqra, links Islam to knowledge and learning, a good link to our own school. Ask pupils to rank which reason matters most.

teach.heading: Why it mattered: for Islam
bullets: It established tawhid as the core message.
It created the first community of believers.
It started the Qur'an, the lasting source of the faith.
teach.note: For a 12-mark Section A answer pupils must reach a judgement. Use the connectives 'this mattered because', 'as a result', 'however'. Note Muslims believe the Qur'an is the final revelation and the Prophet the Seal of the Prophets, covered in a later lesson. Some may argue the first revelation was only the beginning and the later years of preaching and hijrah were also vital.

teach.heading: Hinge question
teach.note: Answer C. A confuses the first revelation with the Hijrah. B is wrong as many verses came later. D: Khadijah's support was important but it is the revelation that started the mission.

check.q: Which is the best reason why the first revelation was important for Islam?
options: It moved the Muslims to Madinah
It began the Prophet's mission and the revelation of the Qur'an
It ended the opposition in Makkah
check.why: The first revelation began the revelation of the Qur'an and the Prophet's mission; the Hijrah and completion of the Qur'an came later.

practice: Put these in order: Khadijah reassures him; Jibril commands him to read; Waraqa confirms; the Prophet returns home frightened.
Write one reason why Khadijah's response mattered.
independent: Core: Describe what happened when the Prophet first received revelation. (4 marks)
Extend: Explain two reasons why the first revelation was important in the establishment of Islam. (6 marks)
Stretch: 'The first revelation was the most important event in the early history of Islam.' Evaluate this view. (12 marks)
exit: Name the angel who brought the revelation.
Return to the big question: give one way one night changed the world.
lessons.homework: Write a paragraph of 5 sentences on why the first revelation mattered, with one quotation-free reference to Khadijah's support.
lessons.send: SEND: timeline cards. EAL: key terms in Arabic with transliteration. Stretch: compare reports and discuss why scholars note differences in details.

lessons.unit: Unit 1.2: The Revelation of the Qur'an
lessons.title: Collecting and preserving the Qur'an: from the Prophet to Uthman
lessons.bigQuestion: How can we be sure the Qur'an we read is the one revealed?
objectives: Describe how the Qur'an was memorised and written in the Prophet's lifetime
Outline the compilation under Abu Bakr and the standard copies under Uthman
successCriteria: All: describe the compilation in order
Most: explain the roles of Abu Bakr, Umar, Zayd and Uthman
Some: evaluate the importance of the standard copies
lessons.crossCurricular: History: preserving texts; how manuscripts are copied
lessons.smsc: Moral: trust (amanah) in guarding the Qur'an

keywords.def: a person who has memorised the Qur'an
sheets on which the Qur'an was written
scribe of the revelation who led the compilation
a bound copy of the Qur'an
the standard copies made under Caliph Uthman

starter: Bismillah. Who was the first caliph?
Why was the Qur'an revealed over 23 years?

teach.heading: In the Prophet's lifetime
bullets: Verses were memorised by many Companions.
Scribes wrote them on parchment, bones, leaves and stones.
The Prophet taught the order of verses and surahs.
teach.note: Explain that the Qur'an was preserved in two ways, memory and writing, and that recitation was passed from teacher to student. Note: the details of which surahs were in written form differ slightly in reports, so use general language. This is a point where verifying statements is useful: the standard Sunni view that the order was divinely guided, based on the Prophet's instruction. Teacher note: every Qur'an reference here is marked verify; check the surah and ayah numbers and the translation against a trusted mushaf and translation before the lesson.

teach.heading: Abu Bakr and the first compilation
teach.note: After the Battle of Yamamah (about 11-12 AH, verify) many Qur'an reciters were killed. Umar feared parts could be lost and urged Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr asked Zayd ibn Thabit, who had written for the Prophet, to collect the Qur'an from written material and from memory, checking with witnesses. Abu Bakr kept the sheets; later they went to Umar, and then to his daughter Hafsa, a wife of the Prophet. Present it as a careful process, not an editing process.

timeline.label: Yamamah
timeline.text: Many reciters killed; concern about loss

timeline.label: Uthman
timeline.text: Standard copies made and sent to major cities

teach.heading: Uthman and the standard copies
bullets: Differences in recitation appeared as Islam spread.
Uthman asked Zayd and a committee to copy from Hafsa's sheets.
Copies were sent to major cities; others were set aside.
teach.note: Explain that Uthman was concerned about disputes over recitation among new Muslims in distant lands. The copies unified the written text. The traditional date is about 650 CE (approx.). Distinguish between collecting (Abu Bakr) and standardising (Uthman); this is a common exam error.

misconception.right: Uthman copied the existing compiled text into standard copies to unite the community

teach.heading: Why this mattered
bullets: It protected the Qur'an from loss.
It prevented disputes over the text.
It supports the belief that the Qur'an is unchanged.
teach.note: Draw out the connection to amanah: Muslims believe they were entrusted to guard the Qur'an. Ask pupils why people today trust the text. Mention that Muslims also continue to memorise the Qur'an, so memory and writing check each other. Encourage balanced answers that identify limitations of reports but stay respectful.

teach.heading: Model answer for the exam
teach.note: Model on the board. Use P-E-E: point, evidence, explain. Stress that evidence should be specific (name Abu Bakr, Zayd, Hafsa, Uthman). If a question asks 'how', describe stages in order.

model.problem: Explain two reasons why the compilation of the Qur'an under Abu Bakr was important. (4 marks)
steps: Reason 1: Many reciters died at Yamamah, so there was a risk of losing parts, and compiling protected the text
Reason 2: Zayd checked written material against memory, which made the collection reliable
Link: this supports the Muslim belief that the Qur'an has been preserved
model.answer: Two developed reasons, each with a link to preservation

teach.heading: Hinge question
teach.note: Answer B. A is Abu Bakr's task. C is wrong because the Prophet did not hold a single book. D confuses the caliphs.

check.q: What was Uthman's main contribution to the Qur'an?
options: He first collected it after Yamamah
He had standard copies made and sent to major cities
He changed the order of the surahs
He wrote down the first verses
check.why: Abu Bakr first compiled the sheets; Uthman standardised copies to avoid disputes over recitation.

practice: Put the events in order: Yamamah; copies sent to cities; Zayd collects the sheets; Hafsa keeps the sheets.
Why did Umar worry after Yamamah?
independent: Core: Describe how the Qur'an was compiled after the Prophet's death. (4 marks)
Extend: Explain two reasons why Uthman made standard copies. (6 marks)
Stretch: 'The compilation under Abu Bakr was more important than the work of Uthman.' Evaluate this view. (12 marks)
exit: Name the scribe who led the first compilation.
Where were the first sheets kept after Umar?
lessons.homework: Write a timeline with 5 stages of the preservation of the Qur'an and add one sentence on why each mattered.
lessons.send: SEND: sequencing cards with pictures. EAL: key names in a glossary. Stretch: explain why both memory and writing mattered.
